correctness.rationale: Every nonempty mixed scale-two clique has at most one vertex in at least one bipartition class. The subcomplexes U and V obtained by attaching one line cone to the full point simplex and vice versa are contractible, with U∩V equal to the incidence graph. The integral Mayer–Vietoris connecting map is an isomorphism H2(K2;Z)→H1(Γ;Z); its defining signed chain inclusion (a,-a) changes sign under color exchange, proving precisely the ε-twist. Counts |E|=(q+1)(q²+q+1), |V|=2(q²+q+1) give q³ free generators. The Fano action is a complete finite computation: all 168 GL3(F2) maps and their 168 polarity composites, 331 Rips faces, full signed Lefschetz sums and an independent oriented-graph-cycle trace agree elementwise. The exact weighted character norm equals 1 over the 336-element group and the character average is zero. The proof covers all finite planes; finite enumeration does not substitute for it.

In the canonical Fano case it supplies an absolutely irreducible full-group character, determines polarity traces and invariant dimensions, and identifies that module with a constituent previously occurring only in a different Heawood matching complex.
